first_impression.reaction: Arrived from a Google search for 'wedding destinations march'. Jumped to the FAQ first, as I always do, and it gave me actual station names, normals periods and a source for the cyclone dates. That's more than most of these listicles bother with, so I went back up and read the entries. The intro didn't oversell anything: 'still that season' is a planner admitting the downside up front. No 'best', no 'award-winning', no 'magical'. I kept reading.

journey.quote: It is early spring in Europe, autumn in New Zealand, and across much of the tropics the closing weeks of the wet or cyclone season, which is still that season.
journey.reaction: Good. They're telling me the catch in the second sentence instead of hiding it under a beach photo.

journey.section: How we chose these ten March destinations
journey.quote: Averaging periods and rain-day definitions also differ between countries, so the [WMO advises care when comparing city climates](https://worldweather.wmo.int/en/city.html?cityId=902): read each place on its own.
journey.reaction: This is the bit that won me over. Someone actually knows you can't line up a 0.1 mm rain day against a 1 mm rain day. That's the kind of caveat I'd put in a spreadsheet footnote.

journey.quote: The [Hellenic National Meteorological Service's climate data for Naxos](http://oldportal.emy.gr/emy/en/climatology/climatology_city?perifereia=South%20Aegean&poli=Naxos) (period not stated by HNMS) gives a March minimum temperature of 10.4°C, a mean of 13.4°C and a maximum of 15.8°C.
journey.reaction: Admitting the period isn't stated, and then 'Naxos is not Santorini or Mykonos', is honest. I can check this link myself, which I will.

journey.quote: Milan is a city station, not a lakeside one, and the page does not define its rain day.
journey.reaction: Again flagging the limitation instead of passing Milan off as Como. Fine by me.

journey.quote: For more reading between venue visits, browse the [Wedded Wonderland magazine](/magazine?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-destinations-march&utm_content=magnet).
journey.reaction: Random detour in the middle of the destination list. Doesn't answer anything I came for. It reads like a traffic grab.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, [Smartraveller](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/destinations/asia/indonesia) puts Indonesia's wet season at usually around October to April, when weather can change quickly.
journey.reaction: Every other entry has station normals, Bali only gets a travel advisory. Not a deal-breaker, but I noticed the gap. If there's no official March figure, say so like you did for Naxos.

journey.quote: It called March the wet season, with rainfall from well below to above average, most stations drier than usual, and 640.3 mm at Rarawai Mill in Ba.
journey.reaction: Mixed reading reported straight, including that most stations were drier. They didn't cherry-pick the scary number or the nice one.

journey.quote: What are the wet-weather and cyclone plans, and will you set them out in writing?
journey.reaction: Useful. These are questions I'd actually send a venue. 'In writing' is the right instinct.

journey.section: Shoulder season weather and a plan B
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Good start, but 'inclusions' of what? The venue package, or your service? It doesn't tell me who's paying the advisor.

journey.quote: Yes, if you plan for a shoulder month: cool early spring in Europe, autumn in New Zealand, or warm, wet weeks in the tropics.
journey.reaction: A flat 'Yes' up front is a sales answer. The rest of the article is more careful than that, so this sounds off.

journey.quote: The Greek islands, Lake Como, the Amalfi Coast, the French Riviera and Portugal all work, with cool evenings and indoor space in the plan.
journey.reaction: 'All work' is a bit glib after you just told me Amalfi venues may be shut and Greek ferries may be cancelled.

journey.section: Plan your March wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, works in your time zone and quotes in AUD, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Fee agreed in writing is the right signal, but it's still 'what's the fee?' and 'do you take a cut from the venue?'. Nothing here tells me how you get paid. That's the question that decides whether I enquire.

unanswered_questions: How is the Wedded Concierge fee worked out: flat, percentage, or something else?
Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from the venues and suppliers it recommends here?
Are the venue prices you quote the same as what I'd pay booking direct?
What does the Wedded Advisor actually do for the fee, and what is extra?
Is there a real March wedding you've planned in any of these places, with the actual budget?
Why does Bali have no official station figures when every other entry does?

turn_offs_found.quote: Yes, if you plan for a shoulder month: cool early spring in Europe, autumn in New Zealand, or warm, wet weeks in the tropics.
turn_offs_found.why: A blanket 'Yes' is a promise, not evidence. The body of the article is carefully hedged; the FAQ answer isn't.

turn_offs_found.quote: The Greek islands, Lake Como, the Amalfi Coast, the French Riviera and Portugal all work, with cool evenings and indoor space in the plan.
turn_offs_found.why: 'All work' overclaims, given the same page says venues may be closed or short-staffed in March.

would_share_with: My fiancee, as a shortlist starting point
Possibly a Reddit thread, for the WMO caveat about comparing rain days

cta_reaction.quote: Torn between a cool European spring and a warm, wet island? Talk it through with [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-destinations-march&utm_content=primary).
cta_reaction.why: At least the CTA comes after the evidence, not before it, so it doesn't annoy me. I'd click through to look at the Concierge page, but I wouldn't fill in a form until I know how the fee works and whether you take a cut from venues. This article doesn't answer that, and it isn't really its job, but it's what stands between me and an enquiry.

top_3_changes: FAQ: replace 'Yes, if you plan for a shoulder month: cool early spring in Europe, autumn in New Zealand, or warm, wet weeks in the tropics.' with 'It can be, if you plan for a shoulder month: cool early spring in Europe, autumn in New Zealand, or warm, wet weeks in the tropics.'

FAQ: replace 'The Greek islands, Lake Como, the Amalfi Coast, the French Riviera and Portugal all work, with cool evenings and indoor space in the plan.' with 'The Greek islands, Lake Como, the Amalfi Coast, the French Riviera and Portugal can all work, if your venue is open on your date and you plan for cool evenings and indoor space.'

Portugal section: remove the mid-list detour 'For more reading between venue visits, browse the [Wedded Wonderland magazine](/magazine?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-destinations-march&utm_content=magnet).' (replace with an empty string), or move it below the FAQ. It interrupts the list and reads like a traffic grab.
